summary.headline: TVS Motor Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% to INR 13,896 crore and operating EBITDA rose 41% to INR 1,779 crore, with margin at 12.8%.
summary.overview: Total volume grew 28% YoY to 1.63 million units, with revenue of INR 13,896 crore (+38%) and PAT of INR 1,174 crore (+51%). Operating EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 12.8%, helped by price increases and cost actions despite a sharp commodity spike linked to the West Asia conflict. International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), and EV sales grew 86%. Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and expects FY27 industry growth in double digits, with capacity expansion to 8.3 million 2W units by Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +51% YoY (INR 1,050 crore); includes ~INR 150 crore fair value gain vs ~INR 28 crore last year

segments.name: 2-wheeler domestic ICE
segments.commentary: Sales grew 21% YoY versus industry growth of 13%. Overall 2W ICE grew 23% against industry growth of 21%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler EV
segments.commentary: Volume rose to 130,000 units from 70,000 in the prior-year quarter, up 86%. June EV penetration was above 10.6%, and management said EV penetration in 3W crossed 40%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler international
segments.commentary: International market ICE sales grew 31%. Africa, Asia and LATAM contributed, with HLX crossing 5 million cumulative units.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: Total sales rose 48% to 67,000 units from 45,000 units.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: Disbursed to over 14 lakh new customers, taking the customer base to about 2.6 crore. Book size grew 19% and PBT rose 16% to INR 283 crore.

segments.name: Norton
segments.commentary: Manx and Atlas production has started, with Atlas rolling out from Hosur in June. Cumulative investment is about INR 2,000 crore to INR 2,500 crore over the last 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be better than Q1; 2W ICE growth could be slightly better than Q1 and EV growth similar or slightly better.
Management expects FY27 industry growth of at least double digits in ICE, with EV growth well above penetration levels of about 10.6%.
International growth expected at the same rate or slightly better in Q2.
Price increases of about 1.5% were taken in Q1 and about 0.5% are planned in Q2, subject to market conditions.
Q3 is the key watch item due to El Nino, the base effect and GST benefits starting late September.
Festive season launches are planned for October and November.
capex_capacity: 2W capacity is planned to rise from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4 FY27, in stages over Q2 and Q3.
3W capacity is planned to rise from about 0.25 million to about 0.42 million units, with a good share in EV.
Total capex, including new products and capacity expansion, is about INR 3,500 crore.
Capacity additions take about 3 to 4 months to commission.
Partnership with IOC for last-mile LPG cylinder distribution and cargo EV mobility.
demand_pricing: Commodity costs rose about 3.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% more in Q2, a total of about 4%; about 30% was passed through as per the last call.
Dealer inventory is kept at 25-30 days, with up to about 30 days during the festive season.
Management says it keeps less than 30 days of stock with dealers and cites JD Power rankings of No. 1 and No. 2 in the scooter category.
Scooter category share is about 40% including ICE and EV.
Production was disrupted in April by supply issues but recovered in May and June.
PLI incentive is about 0.6-0.7% of turnover, and about INR 600 crore of PLI is receivable.
Exports are about 26% of turnover; management aims to grow this materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and how is EV demand developing?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler capacity is about 40,000 units moving to 50,000+. 3W capacity is moving from about 20,000 to 30,000 units, with EV a good share. EV demand is spreading from urban to semi-urban areas, and some buyers are moving from motorcycles to scooters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is TVS gaining share against a competitor discounting in scooters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a broad scooter range, frequent feature upgrades, durability and JD Power rankings. It said dealer stock is kept below 30 days and that retail financing supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity headwind and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the impact was in Q1, with some further pressure from aluminium and oil-linked plastics. Price increases were about 1.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% in Q2, with the rest offset by mix, scale and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV profitability improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV contribution is improving quarter after quarter, but it expects the EV margin to reach the company's target over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall capacity and investment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: 2W capacity is moving from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4, with 3W capacity rising to about 0.42 million. Total investment is about INR 3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Norton strategy, investment and volume ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT) are launching across the UK, Europe, India and later the US. The model uses independent dealers and multi-brand premium outlets, with cumulative investment of about INR 2,000-2,500 crore. Management gave no breakeven volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses decline and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April production loss and supply issues drove some cost control. It said brand spend as a percentage of sales will not change much, and launch costs will add to expenses when new products are introduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 600-700 crore PLI receivable collectible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 600 crore is PLI receivable and is fully collectible, with the government having always supported the scheme.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict (aluminium, steel, oil-linked plastics) and a possible further 0.5% cost pressure in Q2.
Supply chain availability, which was disrupted in April.
Q3 demand risks from El Nino, the high base from last year's GST effect and monsoon progression.
Draft Delhi EV policy may ban ICE 2-wheeler sales from around 2028.
Receivables of about INR 600-700 crore, mainly PLI, that need to be collected.
Norton ramp-up and breakeven volumes, which were not disclosed.
Q1 PBT includes about INR 150 crore of fair value gains that are non-operating.
Deep Vakil asked about gearing and a preference share redemption on 1 September; management did not answer this.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, share gains, exports and Q2, while cautious on commodity costs and Q3 timing. Management was evasive on Norton breakeven volume, PLI receivables and the gearing question.
key_quotes: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 30 basis points at 12.8% during the first quarter and this is against 12.5% last year first quarter.
So, as a year, we should estimate an industry growth of double digit.
Yes, INR 600 crores is about PLI, that's a receivable.

adds.what: 2W capacity rise from ~6.8 million to 8.3 million units/yr, in stages over Q2 and Q3
3W capacity rise from ~0.25 million to ~0.42 million units, with a good share in EV
Norton Atlas rolling out from Hosur (Manx and Atlas production started)

growth.why: Management guides Q2 better than Q1 (2W ICE slightly above Q1's 21%, EV similar or better) and FY27 industry growth of double digits, backed by the 2W capacity rise from ~6.8m to 8.3m units by Q4 FY27 (staged over Q2-Q3, 3-4 month commissioning) and 3W capacity to ~0.42m, though no utilisation figure or order book was given.
